To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the different histories and contexts in the two countries have shaped the more incremental change observed in Botswana in comparison to the more rapid change observed in South Africa.

the different historical and contextual factors in the two countries have led to the development of different educational systems, and the recent educational reforms in both countries are not leading to convergence in educational policy and practice.
educational change processes have been shaped by different histories and contexts in Botswana and in South Africa.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between educational policy and practice, and the role of history in shaping this relationship.
how the contexts and processes of educational change in the two countries have shaped educational policy, and how this has in turn shaped classroom practice.
the ways in which the histories and contexts of change have shaped the more recent educational policies and practices in Botswana and in South Africa.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

Botswana and South African educational policies are converging in the direction of greater standardization and accountability, but that the two countries are doing this from very different starting points.

the differences and similarities between Botswana and South African education systems are the result of different histories of educational change and of different histories of decolonization and political change, as well as of different economic and political conditions.

the two countries have followed similar trajectories in terms of curriculum and assessment policies and processes, while diverging in terms of teacher policies and processes, and that this has much to do with different histories of political change.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

Botswana has a more stable, predictable, and incremental approach to education, while South Africa has a less stable and less incremental approach, with greater emphasis on accountability and evaluation.
while Botswana and South African education systems have been influenced by global trends, the specific histories of the two countries have shaped the nature of educational change.
while Botswana’s educational policies have been more consistent and gradual, South Africa’s have been more disruptive and rapid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the different histories and contexts in Botswana and in South Africa continue to shape the ways in which educational policy changes are made and experienced.
the histories, contexts, and politics of education in Botswana and in South Africa continue to influence the way that educational change is conceptualized, planned for, and implemented.

educational policies are shaped not only by the specific political and economic conditions of the time but also by the legacies of the country's history and the different processes of decolonization and development.
